transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-05-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~46 minutes | Recording: internal Fireflies export
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Head of Platform, Nightingale), Priya Shah (SRE), Liam O'Connor (Security), Aisha Khan (Product)

Summary:
- Discovery focused on reliability, incident tolerance, and multi-region fallback policies across Hosted / Dedicated / Private options.
- Customer is evaluating trade-offs: latency vs cost, single-region with failover vs active-active multi-region, and compliance (data residency, KMS).
- Next steps: pricing and SLA docs, security questionnaire, benchmark run across US+EU, pilot kickoff.

Topics covered: fallback policies, model variant fallbacks, multi-region routing and DNS/anycast considerations, SLA targets and credits, RBAC/SSO/KMS, Private (VPC/on-prem) constraints, Dedicated reserved capacity commitments, canary/rollout strategies.

Action items (captured in CRM): Jordan to send pricing/SLA; Priya to schedule benchmark; Nightingale to send security reqs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. Quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood team, and with me is Priya in SE. Could we go around quick on roles?
[00:10] Carlos (Nightingale): Carlos here, Head of Platform. We run the inference stack for payment scoring and fraud detection.
[00:15] Priya Shah (Customer SRE): Priya Shah, SRE. We care about availability and failover time, obviously.
[00:20] Liam (Security): Liam O'Connor, security. I'll be validating compliance and KMS stuff.
[00:24] Aisha (Product): Aisha, product, looking at user impact and latency SLAs.
[00:28] Jordan: Great. Goal for today is to understand your reliability requirements and talk through how Redwood handles incidents, fallbacks, and multi-region routing across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[00:35] Carlos: High level: we need 99.9% up at the API level during business hours, and ideally under 200ms p95 for scoring calls in the US. We also need EU residency for any EU customer PII.
[00:45] Priya Raman (SE): Thanks. Quick note: Redwood's hosted tier typically targets 99.95% with region-aware routing. For Dedicated you can get stricter SLOs and reserved capacity so you avoid noisy neighbor issues. For Private (VPC/on-prem) you control the infra and we provide the control plane integration.
[01:05] Priya Shah: Can you explain how fallback works if a region goes down? Do requests queue, or failover, or do you fall back to a smaller model?
[01:15] Priya Raman: Sure. We have multiple layered fallbacks. First, smart routing will route to another healthy region if your policy is active-active. If you're active-passive, we can failover DNS to another region with ~30-90s depending on DNS TTL and anycast. For bursty short outages, we support automatic fallback to a compatible model variant (lower-precision or smaller architecture) to keep latency low — that's our model-variant fallback. There's also a queueing/buffering mode at the edge for a few seconds to smooth transient spikes.
[01:44] Carlos: That DNS TTL sounds concerning — 30 to 90 seconds could be visible to users. Do you support anycast or load balancer level failover that would be faster?
[01:53] Priya Raman: We do both. Hosted uses a global front door that leverages anycast and health checks for faster failover. For Dedicated, we can configure an HA proxy layer in front of your GPU pool and do active-active if you provision across regions. Private deployments depend on your networking — for VPC we can support cross-region peering and a similar front-door setup, but that requires network config on your side.
[02:14] Liam: From a security standpoint, if you failover to another region, does data ever leave origin region unencrypted, or hit a different KMS? We have EU keys for EU data.
[02:24] Jordan: Important point. We can pin data to a region and disable cross-region failover for PII — it's a policy option. Alternatively, for active-active with EU residency, we can ensure the EU region uses the EU KMS and we refuse processing outside. We'll include the option in the SLA/pricing doc.
[02:40] Priya Shah: What about SLA credits — what's Redwood's commitment on latency and availability?
[02:45] Jordan: Hosted SLA is 99.95% uptime for API (business hours) with credit tiers for sustained violations; Dedicated has customizable SLOs — typically customers request 99.99% for critical workloads under reserved capacity. We will share the formal SLA and credit calculation in the doc.
[02:59] Aisha: Can you share examples of how fallbacks affect output quality? If you drop to a smaller quantized model, are we likely to see drift in scores?
[03:09] Priya Raman: Good question. For scoring models, quantization and smaller variants can lead to slight drift. We recommend running gating tests (we call them eval prompts) during a POC. We also have automatic regression alerts — if quality drops beyond a threshold, traffic can be routed back or the request can be sent to a secondary model for re- scoring. But for deterministic scoring we usually recommend dedicated capacity and model pinning to avoid runtime fallbacks unless you want the availability tradeoff.
[03:40] Carlos: Timeline and procurement: we want to pilot in US + EU next month. We need pricing and commit options for Dedicated. Also curious about cold start on Dedicated — how long to spin up capacity?
[03:53] Jordan: Dedicated pools are provisioned ahead of time. Cold start for a new instance can be minutes if you need to scale, but with reserved pools and autoscaling policies we keep a buffer to meet throughput. For Private on-prem, it depends on your provisioning. We'll include recommended autoscale thresholds.
[04:10] Priya Raman: For the benchmark we propose: 10k scoring calls/day, p95 target 200ms, simulate region failure and measure failover time and quality drift. We'll run that in both US and EU.
[04:23] Priya Shah: How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching across regions? If context is cached in one region and we failover, won't cold starts be bad?
[04:32] Priya Raman: Right — KV cache lives local to the runtime for latency reasons. On failover you will have cold KV cache in the new region until warmed. We mitigate by tiered caching: hot prefixes are replicated across regions for active-active setups, and we also support pre-warming policies during planned maintenance. For the pilot we can instrument cache warm-up times.
[04:55] Liam: Security checklist — we need SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, SSO via SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration. Also we may require customer-managed keys for the EU region.
[05:08] Jordan: We have SOC 2 Type II, ISO attestations, SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit logs. Customer-managed KMS in Hosted is supported for Dedicated and Private. We'll attach our security pack and the questionnaire.
[05:18] Carlos: Any references for customers using multi-region active-active? We want to see architecture patterns.
[05:22] Priya Raman: Yes, we'll share a short architecture doc and a reference diagram of active-active Dedicated pools across us-west/us-east/eu-west with anycast front door and model pinning.
[05:30] Aisha: On cost: Active-active and replicating caches across regions sounds expensive. If we do active-passive with quick failover, what do you recommend to minimize cost while preserving user experience?
[05:40] Priya Raman: Common pattern: use active-passive with automated failover and low DNS TTL plus a small warm standby in the passive region (a minimal reserved pool) to reduce cold start. Combine that with model-variant fallbacks only for non-critical scoring. That balances cost and availability.
[05:55] Carlos: Procurement will push back on a big Dedicated commit if we can meet 99.9% with Hosted cheaper. Can we do a short Dedicated pilot to validate latency?
[06:02] Jordan: Absolutely. Short Dedicated pilot (4-6 weeks) with an eval discount is typical. We'll include committed and pilot pricing.
[06:10] Priya Shah: For Private (VPC), if we manage the infra, what does happen on Redwood side for control plane access? Do you need inbound connectivity?
[06:18] Priya Raman: For VPC we support a private control plane that communicates over customer-managed peering or private link. You can opt for an air-gapped on-prem package; in those cases we ship a control plane connector that runs inside your network. We'll outline network requirements in the security pack.
[06:30] Liam: Auditing: do you have per-request logs and redactable PII? We need audit trails for scoring decisions for compliance.
[06:38] Jordan: We capture request metadata, latency, token counts, and allow per-request payload logging with retention controls. We also support redaction pipelines and can stream logs to your SIEM.
[06:47] Carlos: Thinking about SLOs again — if you promise 99.95% but an outage is due to a third-party cloud region, how is blame/incidence handled and what credits apply?
[06:57] Jordan: SLA credits are calculated on our control plane and public health checks; if the failure is caused by a third-party provider outside our control, we still work with you for remediation but the credit policy reflects force majeure clauses. We'll send the exact legal language in the SLA.
[07:10] Aisha: For rollout strategies, do you support canary and A/B traffic splits across model versions so we can detect regressions pre-release?
[07:17] Priya Raman: Yes — Canary rollouts and percentage traffic splits are built into our Console. You can tie regressions to eval sets and trigger automated rollback.
[07:25] Jordan: Quick recap: Nightingale needs 99.9% API uptime, p95 200ms US, EU data residency, SOC2+KMS, pilot in US+EU. Redwood will share pricing (Dedicated vs Hosted), SLA doc, security pack, reference architecture, and schedule a benchmark run.
[07:41] Carlos: Sounds good. Couple of small items — can you also include model quantization options and recommended bit widths for scoring models? We care about deterministic behavior.
[07:50] Priya Raman: We'll include quantization profiles and recommendations; for scoring we usually recommend quantization-aware training or int8 with calibration to minimize drift.
[07:58] Jordan: Alright we'll follow up with docs and propose dates for the pilot kickoff. Anything else from Nightingale?
[08:05] Priya Shah: Nothing more here.
[08:07] Liam: No, thanks.
[08:09] Aisha: All good.
[08:11] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll send the materials and lock in the benchmark date.
[08:14] End of recording.
